cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where user-supplied URLs or redirect targets are used in server-side network operations (redirects, HTTP requests, OS commands, DNS) without proper validation, allowing attackers to redirect users to malicious sites, perform SSRF, leak credentials, or execute commands.
guideline_text: Trace externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers into privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access. Report code paths where caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect.

mechanism.missing_guard: caller identity is not established before the privileged action begins
mechanism.name: missing authentication before privileged action
mechanism.sink_shape: privileged commands, administrative state changes, credential operations, or protected data access
mechanism.source_shape: externally reachable requests, RPC messages, management calls, or background command triggers
mechanism.typical_fix: require a validated session, principal, token, or authentication filter before any privileged effect

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use the session's organization to determine trusted servers.
sub_patterns.name: Authorization bypass via user-supplied URL hostname
sub_patterns.root_cause: The system derives the authorization trust domain from the hostname of a user-supplied URL instead of the authenticated session, allowing cross-organization access.
